In Smith v. Jones, the plaintiff, Smith, sued Jones for breach of contract, alleging that Jones failed to honor a handshake agreement promising Smith a 25% share of profits from a joint business venture. Although there was no written contract, Smith presented witness testimony to confirm the agreement's existence and its specific terms. The key legal point involves the enforceability of oral agreements and the sufficiency of witness testimony to prove contract terms in the absence of written documentation.
